summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of paraplegia, neurogenic bladder, diabetes, and chronic constipation was admitted for abdominal and flank pain, nausea, and vomiting. Initial concern for pyelonephritis was ruled out due to normal vital signs, absence of fever, and unremarkable urinalysis. The pain was attributed to constipation, exacerbated by immobility and medication noncompliance. She also had a stage 2 pressure ulcer on her right thigh, lower extremity swelling from a known DVT, and a pruritic rash consistent with bed bug bites. Anticoagulation was restarted with Lovenox and Coumadin due to her history of noncompliance and risk of pulmonary embolism. Her diabetes was managed with insulin inpatient and discharge medications including Metformin and Glipizide. She agreed to follow-up care but left against medical advice before receiving formal discharge instructions.
